answer: Anchor each seat to a published survey mark. Enrolment needs one NGS datasheet: a brass disc weathered sable brown, coordinates fixed to the centimetre. The seed names a quadrangle and a two-hour window; the seat photographs the stamped designation beside a placard with the epoch number and uploads raw GNSS observations. Seats sharing a disc or a crew fold into one vote and forfeit 70,000 POA each. A crew-day runs $1,400 and the archive is finite, so a thousand seats means a thousand walks across the atlas. You can print a summit on any map; standing on the copy is what costs.
